summary: Defines four Sieve email filtering extensions, envelope-dsn, redirect-dsn, envelope-deliverby, and redirect-deliverby. The envelope extensions let a filter read delivery status notification and Deliver-By information from the message envelope, while the redirect extensions let it set them when redirecting a message.

eli5.summary: Mail filters are like rules you give a sorting clerk. This gives the clerk the ability to read and set delivery-notice and deadline instructions on the envelope.

questions: what is the sieve envelope-dsn extension
subtitle: Lets a Sieve mail filter read and set delivery-notification and delivery-deadline settings on the message envelope.

tldr.problem: Base Sieve can only see envelope data from plain SMTP, and its redirect action can only name a new recipient, so filters cannot use or control delivery status notification (DSN) and Deliver-By settings.
tldr.mechanism: Four extensions: envelope-dsn and envelope-deliverby add readable envelope parts to the envelope test, while redirect-dsn and redirect-deliverby add arguments to redirect that set the matching SMTP parameters.
tldr.outcome: A Sieve script can test what notifications or deadlines were requested and can set them on redirected mail, with security notes about unwanted notification messages.

today: RFC 6009 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of these four Sieve extensions.

sections.title: Introduction and Capabilities
sections.content:
Sieve (RFC 5228) is a language for filtering email at or around the time of final delivery. It has no user-controlled loops and cannot run external programs, which makes it suitable for servers where users may not run arbitrary code.

Base Sieve has an envelope test, but it exposes only what regular SMTP provides, not fields added by SMTP extensions. Its redirect action only takes a new recipient address. This RFC fills both gaps for two SMTP extensions: delivery status notifications (DSNs, from RFC 3461) and Deliver-By (from RFC 2852).

The four capability strings are envelope-dsn, redirect-dsn, envelope-deliverby and redirect-deliverby. A script names the ones it needs in require.
sections.eli5: Sieve is a set of rules for sorting your mail. Before, the rules could not read some of the special notes on the envelope or write them. These four add-ons fix that.

sections.title: Reading DSN Fields with envelope-dsn
sections.content:
The envelope-dsn extension defines no new tests or actions. It adds four case-insensitive envelope-part strings to the existing envelope test:

  • notify: the notification conditions (NOTIFY values) for the recipient address used in the SMTP RCPT TO command. Values are NEVER, SUCCESS, FAILURE and DELAY. Each condition in effect is tested separately and any match makes the test succeed. NEVER is never combined with another value.
  • orcpt: the original recipient, with xtext encoding removed.
  • ret: the return-of-content value from MAIL FROM, either FULL or HDRS.
  • envid: the envelope identifier from MAIL FROM, in decoded form.

If the parameter does not exist for the message or recipient, the test fails unconditionally. Specifying an ADDRESS-PART argument with these parts is an error, because none of them has address syntax. With the relational extension (RFC 5231), :count is 1 for orcpt, ret and envid when present and 0 otherwise. For notify it equals the number of conditions, or 0 if the parameter is absent.

The RFC's examples show that checking for SUCCESS among other values is easy, checking that FAILURE is the only value needs a :count test, and orcpt always starts with an address type prefix such as rfc822;.
sections.eli5: This lets the clerk read the notes on the envelope that say when the sender wants to be told about the letter, like a note saying tell me if it arrives or tell me if it fails.

sections.title: Reading Deliver-By Fields with envelope-deliverby
sections.content:
The envelope-deliverby extension adds four envelope parts that match the BY parameter of MAIL FROM defined in RFC 2852, plus an optional :zone tagged argument:

  • bytimeabsolute: the by-time converted to an absolute time in restricted ISO 8601 format (the RFC 3339 date-time form, with upper-case T and Z, and zero offset written as Z).
  • bytimerelative: the integer by-time value as it stands now.
  • bymode: notify or return, matching the mode characters N and R.
  • bytrace: trace or the empty string, depending on whether the T modifier is present.

:zone shifts a bytimeabsolute value to a time zone offset such as +0000 before testing and has no effect on other parts. Without it, the local time zone MUST be used. The test fails unconditionally if there is no BY parameter. As with the DSN parts, an ADDRESS-PART is an error.

The by-time is decremented as the message moves through the transport infrastructure, so a script cannot learn what the originator set. It sees only the time remaining when Sieve runs, and bytimerelative can be negative.
sections.eli5: This lets the clerk see the deadline written on the envelope and how much time is left. The clerk cannot see the original deadline, only what is left, because the clock keeps ticking while the letter travels.

sections.title: Setting DSN Options with redirect-dsn
sections.content:
The redirect-dsn extension adds two arguments to the redirect action: :notify and :ret. The usage becomes redirect [:notify "value"] [:ret "FULL"|"HDRS"] <address: string>.

They set the NOTIFY parameter on the ESMTP RCPT TO and the RET parameter on MAIL FROM. They are honored only if the DSN ESMTP extension is available. When it is not, they MUST be ignored and MUST NOT cause an error.

Because notifications are only useful if the sender address is known, when either argument is given and the envelope sender is not empty, implementations MUST set the envelope sender to the address of the Sieve owner. The RFC's example combines :copy (RFC 3894) with :notify "NEVER" to make a private copy of selected messages with no side effects or error notifications.
sections.eli5: When the clerk forwards a letter, the clerk can now write on the new envelope whether anyone should be told about it. Writing do not tell anyone makes a quiet secret copy.

sections.title: Setting Deadlines with redirect-deliverby
sections.content:
The redirect-deliverby extension adds :bytimerelative or :bytimeabsolute, plus optional :bymode and :bytrace, to redirect.

  • :bytimerelative is a number of seconds within which the message should be delivered. Negative values are not allowed.
  • :bytimeabsolute is an absolute limit in restricted ISO 8601 format.
  • :bymode is notify or return. The default is return.
  • :bytrace turns on message tracing.

Using :bymode or :bytrace without a time argument is an error. The arguments build the BY parameter on MAIL FROM. If Deliver-By is unavailable, handling MUST follow RFC 2852 section 4.1.4. As with redirect-dsn, when a time argument is given and the envelope sender is not empty, the sender MUST be set to the Sieve owner's address.

Example from the RFC: redirect :copy :bytimerelative 600 "cellphone@example.com" sends a copy to a cell phone and times out after 10 minutes.
sections.eli5: The clerk can write a deadline on the forwarded letter, such as deliver this in ten minutes or send it back.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The two envelope extensions expose more envelope information, which the RFC says is not believed to raise security issues beyond those of the base envelope test.

The redirect extensions are the concern. redirect-dsn can cause notification messages that might otherwise not be generated, especially success notifications. Sites that limit who may request success notifications will also need to restrict them in redirect-dsn. redirect-deliverby controls how long the transport keeps trying, which could generate additional notification messages. The underlying Deliver-By extension has a minimum by-time limit, but sites may impose additional minimums on redirect actions. The security considerations of base Sieve also apply.
sections.eli5: If anyone could ask for a note every time a letter arrives, the mailroom could be flooded with notes. So sites may need to limit who can ask.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The RFC registers all four capability names with IANA in the Sieve extensions list: envelope-dsn, envelope-deliverby, redirect-dsn and redirect-deliverby. Each entry cites RFC 6009 and gives the Sieve discussion list as the contact address.
sections.eli5: The four new names are written in an official list so nobody else uses them for something different.

items.label: NOTIFY
items.desc: NEVER, SUCCESS, FAILURE or DELAY; each tested separately.
